messages:
Alex: Anyone using the JS/TS SDK inside Next.js middleware (Edge) recently? Hitting weird runtime errors at deploy time: \u2018ReferenceError: process is not defined\u2019 and sometimes \u2018TypeError: require is not a function\u2019.
Rina: Yup — Next edge bundles are strict ESM/no node builtins. What import path are you using?
Alex: `import rd from '@redwood/inference'` from middleware.ts. The package seems to resolve to CJS at build which pulls in node:crypto and a fetch wrapper that expects node-fetch.
Jon: That's classic. A few patterns that helped us: 1) publish an explicit minimal ESM edge entry like `exports['./edge']` that only uses globalThis APIs, 2) add a small adapter in-app that re-exports from that edge entry, 3) avoid any module-level code that touches `process` or imports `node:` modules.
Alex: Can you show an adapter example? I tried dynamic import but Next warns in middleware.
Rina: Sure — simplest worked for us:
```ts
// lib/edge-rd.ts
export { default } from '@redwood/inference/edge-esm';
```
Then `import rd from '../lib/edge-rd';` in middleware. Keeps static import and makes intent explicit.
Jon: Also ensure your SDK's edge build uses `globalThis.fetch` and `globalThis.crypto.subtle` for HMACs. Avoid branching that imports `node:crypto` at top-level; do lazy runtime-detection inside functions if you must.
Alex: Right now our SDK does `const { createHmac } = require('crypto')` guarded by a check, but SWC still includes it and breaks edge.
Rina: Exactly. Even guarded requires/imports evaluate at module parsing time for bundlers. Move to in-function `await import('node:crypto')` or better yet implement WebCrypto-only code path in the edge build.
Alex: After changing to explicit edge export + adapter I now see `TypeError: fetch is not a function` — SDK's fetch wrapper is trying to use undici. Any recommended pattern?
Jon: Export an edge-specific fetch shim that is just `export default globalThis.fetch` for the edge build. For other builds, use runtime detection. Also publish a small README snippet for Next middleware showing `export const config = { runtime: 'edge' }`.
Alex: TS types are complaining because our example repo uses older tsconfig (module commonjs). Suggestion?
Rina: Include a short tsconfig snippet in SDK examples for edge projects: `{"compilerOptions": {"module": "esnext", "target": "es2022", "lib": ["es2022", "dom"]}}`. Also add an `types` entry in the edge export so editors pick up the right types.
Jon: One more gotcha: reading env inside modules. SWC replaces `process.env.X` at build-time but `process` doesn't exist at runtime. For auth, prefer extracting token from `Request` headers inside middleware and pass it to the SDK call.
Alex: Good call. We'll switch to passing tokens via headers rather than module-level env reads.
cli-bot: Action: open SDK ticket to add `exports['./edge']` + edge README snippet.
DocsBot: Suggestion: add example middleware with adapter + tsconfig + note about WebCrypto fallback. Could copy the adapter snippet into the README.
Alex: I'll open a PR that adds `edge-esm` build, adapter example, and a tiny docs section explaining the pitfalls (process, node:crypto, fetch wrapper). Will ping when ready.
Rina: If you paste the failing stack trace here I can draft a minimal patch to lazy-load node:crypto only in non-edge builds.
Alex: Will do. Thanks all!
